new.s: In APPSC 2021, the Cuddapah system of rocks was keyed as being mainly composed of which one of the following?
new.x: The Cuddapah system (Purana, ~1,400-600 million years) is sedimentary - shale, slate, quartzite and limestone; shales and slates are clay rocks, so the key was 'clay'. Basalt is the Deccan Trap rock, granite is typical of the Archaean, and coal belongs to the Gondwana system.
new.tq: Cuddapah = sedimentary Purana; shale and slate = clay rocks.

new.s: Which one of the following is a young fold mountain range?
new.x: The Alps are young (Tertiary/Alpine) fold mountains. The Aravallis are very old Precambrian fold mountains, and the Appalachians and Urals are old Palaeozoic fold mountains.
new.tq: APPSC G2 2024: among Appalachians, Aravallis, Alps, Urals, only the Alps are young.

new.s: Which one of the following is NOT a young fold mountain?
new.x: The Sierra Nevada is a block (fault) mountain, though it often appears in 'young folded' lists. The Andes, Rockies and Himalaya are young Tertiary fold mountains.

new.s: Which one of the following statements about P-waves (primary waves) is correct?
o: They are transverse waves that travel only through solids.
They arrive first and travel through solids, liquids and gases with push-pull motion.
They travel only along the Earth's surface and cause the most damage.
They are the slowest seismic waves and are stopped by the outer core.
new.x: P-waves are the fastest and arrive first; they are longitudinal (compressional, push-pull) and pass through solids, liquids and gases. Transverse waves confined to solids are S-waves; surface (L) waves travel along the surface, arrive last and cause most damage; it is S-waves that the liquid outer core stops.
new.tq: P = primary = push-pull = passes everything; S = shear = solids only.

new.s: White Island (Whakaari), a volcano that erupted in December 2019, is located in which country?
new.x: White Island (Whakaari) is in New Zealand and erupted in December 2019. Indonesia has Krakatoa and Dukono, Japan has Fujiyama and Mount Aso, and the Philippines has Taal and Mayon.
new.tq: Whakaari = Maori name; New Zealand, Dec 2019 (APPSC PYQ).
